intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August 2026 from Seattle

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing your family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional games, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the island.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing day at one of Maui's most famous and family-friendly beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand. Enjoy swimming, boogie boarding, and building sandcastles while watching cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside vendors and nearby restaurants make it easy to spend the whole day without leaving the area.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a spectacular light show. The Junior Ranger program keeps kids engaged and educational, making it a memorable family adventure unlike anything else on Earth.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food with a self-guided food tour hitting local favorites like Rainbow Drive-In and Helena's Hawaiian Food. Sample iconic dishes including loco moco, kalua pork, poi, haupia, and shave ice from legendary spots like Matsumoto's. An affordable and delicious way to introduce the whole family to the true flavors of Hawaii beyond resort dining.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Honolulu Airport at 22:30. Collect luggage, arrange shuttle or TheBus (most budget-friendly option, ~$3/person) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. Pick up light snacks from a nearby 7-Eleven or ABC Store if hungry.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snacks
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport snacks
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport before baggage claim or a convenience store near the hotel (~$5–$10)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — it's a late arrival. Confirm check-in arrangements with Aegean Bliss Resort in advance since you'll arrive after 10 PM. Download the DaBus2 app for TheBus routes to save on transport throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a relaxed wake-up, head down to the beachfront at your resort. Take a morning stroll along the shoreline, collect shells, and enjoy the sunrise over the Pacific. Free and beautiful way to start your Hawaiian adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local neighborhood on foot. Find a nearby beach park (many are free) and set up for an afternoon of swimming, snorkeling with rented gear (~$10–$15), and sandcastle building with the kids. Pick up sunscreen and beach supplies at a local ABC Store to save vs. resort prices.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the beach — a quintessential Hawaiian experience at no cost. Head back to the resort area for a casual dinner at a nearby plate lunch spot or food truck.

meals.breakfast: Grab groceries from a local supermarket (Foodland or Times Supermarket) — yogurt, fruit, and granola bars (~$8–$12 for the family)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from the supermarket — sandwiches, chips, and fruit (~$10–$15)
meals.dinner: Local plate lunch restaurant or food truck near the resort — loco moco or teriyaki chicken plates (~$10–$14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Stop at a Foodland or Times Supermarket today to stock up on breakfast items, snacks, and drinks for the week — this is the single biggest money-saving move for a budget Hawaii trip. Budget ~$60–$80 for a week's worth of breakfast and snack supplies.

day_by_day.morning: Kaanapali Beach Family Day (Featured Experience): Head to Kaanapali Beach, one of Maui's most iconic and family-friendly stretches of coastline. Arrive early to claim a great spot. The kids will love the calm, clear waters perfect for swimming. Walk the Kaanapali Beachfront Path (~1.5 miles) for stunning ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying Kaanapali Beach — look for sea turtles near Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a), a famous free snorkeling spot right on the beach. Rent snorkel gear from a local shop (~$10–$15/set) rather than through resort concierge. Build sandcastles and enjoy the warm afternoon sun.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the free cliff diving ceremony at Black Rock at sunset — a Maui tradition that is completely free to watch and very memorable for kids. Head to Lahaina town for dinner and a stroll through the historic waterfront area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast from supermarket supplies — fruit, cereal, and juice (~$3–$5 per person)
meals.lunch: Pack a cooler lunch to the beach — PB&J sandwiches, chips, fruit, and water (~$10–$15 total)
meals.dinner: Aloha Mixed Plate in Lahaina — famous local spot with affordable Hawaiian plates, ocean views. Macaroni salad, kalua pork, and rice (~$12–$16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Parking at Kaanapali can be expensive ($20–$30/day in resort lots). Look for free street parking in Lahaina and walk or take the free Kaanapali Trolley. Apply reef-safe sunscreen generously — the Maui sun is intense. Bring plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a free or low-cost local beach park. Many neighborhood beach parks across Hawaii offer free parking, restrooms, and picnic tables. Spend the morning swimming, playing beach volleyball, or simply relaxing. These spots are where locals go and are often less crowded than tourist beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local farmers market if one is running (many operate on weekday afternoons and weekends). Pick up fresh tropical fruits like lilikoi, starfruit, and locally grown mangoes at very low prices. Great cultural experience and a way to try Hawaiian produce affordably.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the resort for a relaxed evening. Use the resort's pool and facilities. After dinner, do a short family stargazing session on the beach — Hawaii has some of the clearest skies in the world away from city lights.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast — scrambled eggs if you have access to a kitchenette, or cereal and fruit (~$3–$5 per person)
meals.lunch: Farmers market finds — fresh fruit, local snacks, and a shave ice treat (~$10–$15 total)
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal if your room has a kitchenette (pasta or rice with protein from the supermarket, ~$15–$20 total) OR pick up affordable poke bowls from a local grocery store deli (~$10–$13 per bowl)

day_by_day.notes: Check local Hawaii event calendars (gohawaii.com or local Facebook groups) for free community events, hula performances, or cultural demonstrations happening this week. Many resorts and shopping centers host free evening shows.

day_by_day.morning: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration (Featured Experience — travel day to Big Island or explore volcanic geology locally): If staying on Maui, visit Haleakalā National Park instead — a stunning volcanic crater accessible for ~$30/vehicle (covers 3 days). Drive up to the summit area for incredible views. Start early as clouds roll in by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Haleakalā's lower Kīpahulu district if accessible, or hike the Sliding Sands Trail partway into the crater (free with park entry). The alien landscape is unlike anything else on Earth and fascinates kids and adults alike. Bring layers — it gets cold at the summit.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back down and stop in the charming upcountry town of Makawao for a browse and early dinner. Then return to the resort for a restful evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the drive — hotel room supplies or a quick stop at a local bakery in Paia town (~$5–$8 per person)
meals.lunch: Pack a full picnic lunch — sandwiches, trail mix, fruit, and lots of water. No food services inside the park, and outside options are limited (~$10–$15 total)
meals.dinner: Makawao town — Rodeo General Store or a local diner with affordable plate lunches (~$10–$15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: If the group is on Oahu, substitute with a visit to Diamond Head State Monument ($5/person) and Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve ($25/adult, free for kids under 13) for a volcano-meets-beach experience. Bring jackets for Haleakalā — summit temps can be 30–40°F even in August.

day_by_day.morning: Free beach morning — revisit your favorite beach from earlier in the trip or try a new one. Many of Hawaii's best beaches are completely free to access. Try boogie boarding (rent boards for ~$5–$10/hour) or just enjoy the waves and sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a free cultural or historical site. Options include: Iao Valley State Monument (free entry, stunning needle rock formation), historic plantation towns, or a Hawaiian heiau (ancient temple site). These offer great educational value for kids and are completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Luau research night — look for a free or low-cost luau alternative. Some resorts and community centers host free hula and cultural performances. Check Old Lahaina Luau (splurge option ~$130/adult) or look for community hula shows at shopping centers which are completely free.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast from supermarket supplies (~$3–$5 per person)
meals.lunch: Beach picnic — deli sandwiches and drinks from Foodland (~$10–$15 total)
meals.dinner: Maui Tacos or a local Mexican-Hawaiian fusion spot — affordable, filling, and family-friendly (~$10–$13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Midway through the trip is a good time to do a laundry run if needed. Many laundromats are affordable (~$5–$8 per load). Also restock supermarket supplies for the second half of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling adventure at a top-rated free snorkeling beach. Kapalua Bay (Maui) or Hanauma Bay (Oahu) offer spectacular marine life. Rent gear if you don't have it (~$10–$15). Kids will be amazed by the colorful fish, sea turtles, and coral. Arrive early for the best visibility and fewer crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snorkeling, relax on the beach and enjoy the afternoon. Walk to a nearby tide pool area if available — great for kids to explore starfish, sea urchins, and small marine creatures at no cost. Bring water shoes for rocky areas.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a casual beach walk at golden hour. Look for a free hula performance or live music at a nearby resort lobby or shopping center (many offer free nightly entertainment). End the night with shave ice from a local stand — a Hawaiian staple.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast — toast, fruit, and eggs if kitchenette available (~$3–$5 per person)
meals.lunch: Beachside picnic or nearby food truck — fish tacos or spam musubi (~$8–$12 total)
meals.dinner: Local ramen or noodle shop for a budget-friendly, hearty dinner (~$10–$14 per person). Try Ichiban or a local Japanese restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: Shave ice is a must-try Hawaiian experience — budget ~$4–$6 per person. Matsumoto Shave Ice on Oahu's North Shore is legendary. Ask for it with azuki beans and ice cream for the full local experience.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a local hiking trail appropriate for families. Hawaii has many free, well-maintained trails with stunning views. Options include: Manoa Falls Trail (Oahu, free), Twin Falls (Maui, free), or any number of coastal walks. Bring plenty of water and wear sturdy shoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cool off at the beach after the hike. Spend the afternoon swimming and playing in the waves. If kids need a change of pace, look for a local playground near the beach — many coastal parks have excellent free playgrounds with ocean views.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local night market or swap meet if one is scheduled (many run on weekends and offer cheap local food, crafts, and entertainment). Otherwise, enjoy a quiet resort evening with a movie night in the room.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the hike — hotel room supplies or a local bakery (~$5–$8 per person)
meals.lunch: Pack trail snacks and a picnic lunch to eat after the hike at the beach — easy sandwiches and fruit (~$10–$15 total)
meals.dinner: Local Hawaiian BBQ or plate lunch spot — kalbi ribs, macaroni salad, and rice (~$12–$15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Always check trail conditions before hiking in Hawaii — rain can make trails slippery quickly. The AllTrails app is free and has detailed info on difficulty levels, length, and current conditions for all major Hawaii trails.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day — return to your favorite beach of the trip. Spend the morning soaking in the last of the Hawaiian sun, swimming, and enjoying the ocean. Let the kids play freely and take lots of photos to remember the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping on a budget — skip the resort gift shops and head to local markets, swap meets, or discount stores. ABC Stores offer affordable Hawaii-themed souvenirs. Look for locally made macadamia nuts, Kona coffee, and sea salt as authentic, affordable gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Special farewell dinner — slightly splurge on a nicer local restaurant for a memorable last dinner in Hawaii. Look for early bird specials or happy hour menus to keep costs down. Enjoy one last Hawaiian sunset on the beach as a family.

meals.breakfast: Hotel room breakfast — use up remaining supermarket supplies (~$3–$5 per person)
meals.lunch: One last plate lunch from a favorite local spot discovered during the trip (~$10–$14 per person)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range local restaurant with ocean views — look for early bird specials (~$18–$25 per person). Consider Duke's, a classic Hawaii chain with beautiful settings and reasonable prices.

day_by_day.notes: Use up perishable supermarket supplies today in breakfast and snacks to avoid waste. Pack souvenirs carefully — macadamia nuts and coffee are TSA-friendly. Check airline baggage policies if you've picked up extra items during the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for one final sunrise on the beach — a peaceful and free send-off from Hawaii. Pack up your room, double-check for forgotten items, and do a final sweep of the resort. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort per their checkout time (typically 11 AM).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport with plenty of time — aim to arrive 2–3 hours before your flight for international/mainland departures. If you have time before needing to leave for the airport, take a final short beach walk or grab a last shave ice near the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with wonderful memories, a tan, and a suitcase full of aloha. Review your trip budget and celebrate staying within your budget while having an incredible family vacation in paradise!

meals.breakfast: Light hotel room breakfast using last supplies — granola bars, fruit (~$3–$5 per person)
meals.lunch: Airport food (budget ~$12–$18 per person) or pack snacks from remaining supermarket supplies for the flight
meals.dinner: On the plane or at a layover airport

day_by_day.notes: Budget recap tip: The biggest savings on this trip come from supermarket breakfasts (~$60–$80 saved vs. eating out), using TheBus or free shuttles (~$40–$60 saved), packing picnic lunches (~$80–$100 saved), and choosing free beaches and hikes over paid attractions. A family of 4 can comfortably enjoy 10 days in Hawaii for $200–$300/day total (excluding flights and hotel) with careful planning.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport at 22:30. Collect luggage, arrange ground transportation (pre-book a shuttle or rideshare to save costs), and check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Unwind with a light snack and get settled into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport
meals.dinner: Grab a late-night bite at the hotel bar or a nearby 24-hour spot like Zippy's — a beloved local chain open late serving Hawaiian comfort food

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Pre-download offline maps and confirm resort check-in details ahead of time. Tip: exchange some cash before leaving the airport for easier tipping and small purchases.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Take a slow stroll along the beachfront to get your bearings, dip your toes in the ocean, and soak in your first full Hawaiian sunrise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a nearby beach close to the resort for a relaxed family afternoon. Rent snorkel gear from a local beach shack and try shallow-water snorkeling just off the shore. Build sandcastles, swim, and enjoy the warm Pacific waters at your own pace.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the resort's beachfront area. Explore the nearby hotel strip for a casual dinner and pick up any essentials from a local ABC Store or grocery.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet or on-site café — budget around $15–$20 per person
meals.lunch: Beachside food truck or shave ice stand — try a classic Hawaiian shave ice with azuki beans
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki or a similar mid-range oceanfront restaurant — try the Hula Pie dessert and fresh catch of the day (~$25–$40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is your recovery and orientation day. Don't over-schedule. Apply reef-safe sunscreen — it's required at many Hawaii beaches and protects the coral.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — arrive early (7:00–8:00 AM) to beat the crowds and secure a parking spot. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then snorkel through crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral. A truly unmissable family experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by early afternoon. Spend the afternoon relaxing at the resort pool or beachfront. Let the kids decompress while parents enjoy a tropical cocktail. Optional: rent stand-up paddleboards from the resort or a nearby vendor.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the local neighborhood on foot. Browse shops, watch street performers, and enjoy the lively evening atmosphere near your resort area.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort or grab a smoothie bowl from a nearby café before heading to Hanauma Bay
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch or purchase snacks at Hanauma Bay's snack bar (limited options — packing food recommended)
meals.dinner: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch experience at a local diner like Rainbow Drive-In — try the loco moco or kalua pork plate (~$12–$18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations — book online at least 2 days ahead. Entry fee is around $25 per adult; children under 13 are free. Bring water shoes as the sandy entry can have some rocky patches.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour — embark on a self-guided food tour of Oahu's most iconic local eateries. Start with a classic breakfast plate at a local diner, then work your way through neighborhoods sampling poi, spam musubi, saimin noodle soup, and fresh poke bowls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bishop Museum or Iolani Palace for a family-friendly dose of Hawaiian history and culture. These are excellent indoor options if the afternoon gets hot, and both are engaging for kids and adults alike.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Chinatown or the Ala Moana area. Browse local boutiques and pick up Hawaiian souvenirs. Enjoy a relaxed evening back at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Part of the food tour — try a Portuguese malasada from Leonard's Bakery, a Honolulu institution
meals.lunch: Continue the food tour — poke bowl from Ono Seafood or a plate lunch from Yama's Fish Market (~$12–$20)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at a local family restaurant — try Zippy's for Hawaiian comfort food or Kono's for a hearty plate (~$15–$25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The food tour is self-guided so you can move at your own pace — perfect for families with young children. Bring a small cooler bag if you want to save leftovers. Iolani Palace requires advance tickets; book online.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit — spend a full day immersing your family in the traditions of six Polynesian cultures: Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa (New Zealand). Start with the morning village tours where costumed guides demonstrate fire-making, coconut husking, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center. Watch the afternoon canoe pageant on the waterway — a spectacular free-flowing cultural parade. Let the kids try hands-on activities like spear throwing and hula dancing lessons.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the world-famous Ha: Breath of Life evening show — a breathtaking Polynesian luau-style dinner and live performance featuring fire dancers, acrobats, and traditional music. This is a highlight of any Hawaii family trip.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departing — the Cultural Center is about 35 miles from Honolulu
meals.lunch: Gateway Buffet at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included in most package tickets, featuring island-inspired dishes (~included in ticket price)
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau dinner package at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included with evening show package (~$120–$160 per adult, $80–$100 per child)

day_by_day.notes: Book Polynesian Cultural Center tickets well in advance — they sell out quickly in summer. Allow a full day (9 AM–9 PM). The drive from Honolulu takes about 45–60 minutes; consider renting a car for this day or booking a shuttle package.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning after the long Cultural Center day. Sleep in, enjoy a relaxed resort breakfast, and spend the morning by the pool or beach. Let the family recharge at a comfortable pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a family hike to Diamond Head State Monument — a moderate 1.6-mile round-trip trail leading to stunning panoramic views of Waikiki and the Pacific Ocean. The hike takes about 1.5 hours and is suitable for older children. Younger kids may need assistance on steeper sections.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a sunset dinner cruise or simply watch the sunset from the beach. The evening light over the ocean from Oahu's south shore is spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Relaxed resort breakfast or a nearby café — try açaí bowls or fresh tropical fruit plates
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch packed from a nearby Foodland or Times Supermarket before the Diamond Head hike — save money and enjoy a scenic summit snack
meals.dinner: Mid-range beachside restaurant — try Hula Grill Waikiki or a similar spot for fresh fish tacos and Hawaiian-inspired dishes (~$30–$45 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Head entry is $5 per person or $10 per vehicle. Arrive before 2 PM to avoid afternoon heat and crowds. Bring plenty of water and wear closed-toe shoes for the hike. The summit tunnel sections are narrow — exciting for kids!

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight to Maui (book in advance — Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest offer frequent short flights, ~30–45 minutes, ~$80–$150 per person each way). Check in to a Maui accommodation or arrange a day trip. Head straight to Kaanapali Beach upon arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — spend the afternoon at one of Maui's most iconic and family-friendly beaches. The calm, clear waters are perfect for swimming and snorkeling. Rent beach chairs and umbrellas, try boogie boarding, and look for sea turtles resting on the sand.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the legendary Cliff Dive Ceremony at Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) at sunset — a free nightly tradition where a torch lighter dives off the volcanic rock into the ocean. A magical family moment. Enjoy dinner along the Kaanapali strip.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the resort before heading to the airport — or grab a smoothie at the Honolulu airport
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Leilani's on the Beach or Hula Grill Kaanapali — fresh fish, burgers, and salads with ocean views (~$20–$35 per person)
meals.dinner: Casual dinner at Dukes Beach House Maui or a local plate lunch spot along Front Street in Lahaina (~$25–$40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a day-trip or overnight extension to Maui. If budget allows, consider staying one night in Maui to reduce travel fatigue. Book inter-island flights at least 3–4 weeks in advance for best prices. Kaanapali Beach parking can fill up — arrive before 10 AM or use resort beach access.

day_by_day.morning: If staying overnight in Maui: explore the Road to Hana highlights — visit Twin Falls waterfall (easy 10-minute walk), pick up fresh banana bread from a roadside stand, and enjoy the lush tropical scenery. Alternatively, visit the Maui Ocean Center aquarium — excellent for families with younger children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return flight to Oahu (or continue Maui exploration). Back at Aegean Bliss Resort, enjoy a relaxed afternoon at the beach. Try a new water activity — outrigger canoe paddling or a beginner surf lesson available from most Waikiki beach vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Low-key evening at the resort. Enjoy the resort amenities, play beach games at sunset, and have an early dinner to rest up for the upcoming Big Island adventure.

meals.breakfast: Maui roadside smoothie or açaí bowl from a local café
meals.lunch: Roadside banana bread and fresh fruit from local Maui farm stands (budget-friendly and delicious)
meals.dinner: Back on Oahu — try a local Hawaiian BBQ spot or the resort restaurant for a relaxed family dinner (~$20–$35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is a full-day experience if done properly — only attempt it if you have a full morning and a rental car. The Maui Ocean Center is a great alternative for families with younger children (tickets ~$30 adult, $20 child). Book in advance online.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight to the Big Island (Kona or Hilo airport). Head to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park — one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes. Begin with the Kilauea Visitor Center to get oriented, then walk the Crater Rim Trail for dramatic views of the Halemaumau Crater.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Hawaii Volcanoes National Park. Walk through the Thurston Lava Tube — a naturally formed underground tunnel that kids absolutely love. Drive Chain of Craters Road for sweeping views of ancient lava flows meeting the ocean. Look for lava entry points if active flows are accessible.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the visitor area at dusk — the glowing lava lake inside Halemaumau Crater is most visible and spectacular after dark. This is one of the most awe-inspiring natural spectacles on Earth. Return to Hilo or Kona for overnight stay (or fly back to Oahu if doing a day trip).

meals.breakfast: Airport breakfast or pack snacks for the flight and early park arrival
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch from a Hilo grocery store (KTA Super Stores) before entering the park — limited food options inside
meals.dinner: Hilo town dinner at Cafe Pesto or Seaside Restaurant — fresh local fish and farm-to-table Hawaiian cuisine (~$25–$40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park entry is $35 per vehicle (valid 7 days). Check the USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory website before your visit for current eruption activity updates. Bring layers — the park sits at 4,000 feet elevation and can be cool and misty. Volcanic fumes (vog) can be irritating — those with respiratory conditions should take precautions.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — return to Oahu if needed or enjoy a final Big Island experience. If back at Aegean Bliss Resort, take one last sunrise beach walk. Swim in the ocean one final time, collect a few shells, and soak in the beauty of your beachfront surroundings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely checkout from the resort (request late checkout if available). Do any last-minute souvenir shopping at the International Market Place or local boutiques. Pick up Hawaiian coffee, macadamia nuts, and local honey as gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport with plenty of time. Enjoy a final Hawaiian meal before your departure — make it memorable.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — treat yourself to a full spread to celebrate a wonderful trip
meals.lunch: Farewell plate lunch at a beloved local spot — try Helena's Hawaiian Food (a James Beard Award-winning institution) for authentic poi, laulau, and pipikaula (~$15–$20 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or early dinner near the airport — Honolulu Airport has decent dining options including local Hawaiian favorites

day_by_day.notes: Daniel K. Inouye International Airport recommends arriving 3 hours before international flights and 2 hours before domestic. Return your rental car with a full tank to avoid extra fees. Pack any fresh fruit or agricultural products carefully — Hawaii has strict rules about what can leave the islands. Mahalo for a wonderful trip!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing your family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional games, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the island.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing day at one of Maui's most famous and family-friendly beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand. Enjoy swimming, boogie boarding, and building sandcastles while watching cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside vendors and nearby restaurants make it easy to spend the whole day without leaving the area.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a spectacular light show. The Junior Ranger program keeps kids engaged and educational, making it a memorable family adventure unlike anything else on Earth.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food with a self-guided food tour hitting local favorites like Rainbow Drive-In and Helena's Hawaiian Food. Sample iconic dishes including loco moco, kalua pork, poi, haupia, and shave ice from legendary spots like Matsumoto's. An affordable and delicious way to introduce the whole family to the true flavors of Hawaii beyond resort dining.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Honolulu Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in to your Beachfront suite, enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the resort (tropical fruit platter, sparkling wine, and fresh lei greeting). Wind down with a moonlit stroll along the private beach.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or airport dining
meals.lunch: In-flight or airport dining
meals.dinner: Light late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort — recommended: fresh poke bowl, macadamia-crusted ahi tuna bites, and tropical fruit smoothies available 24/7 for arriving guests

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Resort concierge should be notified of late arrival. Keep Day 2 light to allow the family to recover from travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late start — enjoy a luxurious breakfast at the resort's oceanfront restaurant. Spend the morning relaxing at the Aegean Bliss Resort's private beachfront: lounge chairs, cabana service, and calm morning waves perfect for the family. Optional: gentle swim in the resort's infinity pool overlooking the Pacific.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and vibrant coral. Book a premium guided snorkeling experience with private instructor for the family, including top-of-the-line snorkel gear rental, educational briefing, and a guided underwater tour. Reservations required; book the exclusive early afternoon slot to avoid peak crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for sunset cocktails at the beachfront bar. Enjoy a premium sunset dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring locally sourced Hawaiian seafood and farm-to-table cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Oceanfront breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict with kalua pork, Kona coffee, and fresh-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Light picnic-style lunch prepared by the resort and packed for Hanauma Bay — gourmet sandwiches, fresh fruit, hydration packs
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort signature restaurant — recommended: whole-roasted Hawaiian snapper, lobster bisque, and Kona chocolate lava cake for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations (book online). Arrive early afternoon to secure parking. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only — it is required by Hawaii state law. Children must be supervised at all times in the water.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour — Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food with a curated, luxury-guided food tour hitting iconic local favorites such as plate lunch spots, shave ice stands, and poke bars across Honolulu. A private guide will escort the family, sharing the cultural history behind each dish including laulau, kalua pig, lomi salmon, haupia, and garlic shrimp.
day_by_day.afternoon: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit — Spend the afternoon immersing your family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa. Enjoy canoe rides, traditional craft workshops, fire-making demonstrations, and cultural performances. Upgrade to the Ali'i Luau VIP package for preferred seating and exclusive backstage access.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the Polynesian Cultural Center's spectacular evening show 'Ha: Breath of Life' — a world-class theatrical performance with fire dancers, drummers, and traditional storytelling. VIP seating with premium dinner package included.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — Hawaiian açaí bowls, macadamia nut pancakes, fresh mango, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour — curated tastings across multiple local eateries (included in tour experience)
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau VIP dinner at Polynesian Cultural Center — traditional imu-roasted kalua pig, poi, fresh seafood, tropical desserts, and unlimited beverages

day_by_day.notes: Book Polynesian Cultural Center tickets and Ali'i Luau well in advance — VIP packages sell out quickly. Private transportation recommended for the full day. The Cultural Center is approximately 35 miles from Honolulu; allow 45–60 minutes travel time each way.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury catamaran sailing excursion along the Oahu coastline — depart from Honolulu Harbor on a chartered private catamaran with a dedicated crew. Enjoy dolphin watching, snorkeling stops, and stunning views of Diamond Head from the water. Champagne breakfast served on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Diamond Head State Monument — hike the iconic volcanic crater trail (approximately 1.6 miles round trip) for panoramic views of Honolulu and Waikiki. Hire a private guide for an enriched historical and geological narrative. Suitable for families with children aged 6 and above.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at a top Honolulu fine-dining restaurant — reserve a table at a renowned oceanfront establishment such as Orchids at Halekulani or MW Restaurant for an elevated Hawaiian culinary experience.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast served on the private catamaran — smoked salmon, croissants, tropical fruits, mimosas, and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch at Diamond Head State Monument — resort-prepared bento boxes with premium Hawaiian ingredients
meals.dinner: Orchids at Halekulani or comparable luxury restaurant — recommended: butter-poached Maine lobster, pan-seared Kona kampachi, and lilikoi soufflé

day_by_day.notes: Private catamaran charter should be booked at least 2 weeks in advance. Diamond Head hike is moderately strenuous — wear comfortable shoes and bring plenty of water. Best hiking time is before 10:00 AM to avoid heat; afternoon timing is acceptable if catamaran runs long.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight from Honolulu (HNL) to Maui (OGG) — depart on a morning Hawaiian Airlines or Mokulele Airlines premium cabin flight. Private luxury SUV transfer from Kahului Airport to Kaanapali Beach area. Check in to a reserved premium suite or day-use luxury villa near Kaanapali.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — Spend a relaxing afternoon at one of Maui's most famous and family-friendly beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand. Enjoy private cabana service, paddleboarding, boogie boarding, and snorkeling at Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a), a legendary snorkeling spot teeming with sea turtles and tropical fish. Private beach butler service available.
day_by_day.evening: Witness the iconic Cliff Diving Ceremony at Black Rock at sunset — a traditional Hawaiian ritual performed nightly at the Sheraton Maui. Enjoy a premium sunset cocktail reception on the beach followed by dinner at a top Kaanapali restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure — continental spread, pastries, and Kona coffee to go
meals.lunch: Beachside luxury lunch at Kaanapali — private catered spread with fresh poke, lobster rolls, tropical salads, and coconut water delivered to your cabana
meals.dinner: Japengo at Hyatt Regency Maui or Leilani's on the Beach — recommended: fresh island fish, wagyu beef, and Hawaiian-inspired desserts with ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights and Kaanapali cabana reservations in advance. Bring reef-safe sunscreen and water shoes for Black Rock snorkeling. The Cliff Diving Ceremony begins at sunset — arrive 20 minutes early for best viewing spots.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise Road to Hana luxury driving tour — embark on a private guided journey along Maui's legendary Road to Hana (Hana Highway), stopping at the most breathtaking viewpoints including Twin Falls, Garden of Eden Arboretum, Wailua Falls, and black sand beaches. Private luxury SUV with expert local guide narrating the cultural and natural history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana experience — visit Wai'anapanapa State Park's stunning black sand beach, explore lava tubes, and enjoy a private picnic lunch in a secluded rainforest clearing. Optional: short hike to a hidden waterfall swimming hole for the adventurous family members.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kaanapali for a relaxing evening. Enjoy a private in-suite Hawaiian spa experience — couples and family massage packages with traditional lomilomi techniques, volcanic stone therapy, and botanical treatments delivered to your suite.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before departure — acai bowls, eggs, fresh tropical fruits, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Private gourmet picnic in the rainforest along Road to Hana — curated by a local chef with fresh island ingredients, artisan cheeses, charcuterie, and tropical fruits
meals.dinner: In-suite private dining experience — curated 4-course Hawaiian tasting menu prepared and served by a private chef in your suite

day_by_day.notes: Road to Hana is approximately 65 miles one way with over 600 curves — depart by 7:00 AM for the best experience. Motion sickness medication recommended for children prone to car sickness. Wai'anapanapa State Park requires advance reservations. Allow 10–12 hours for the full round-trip experience.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight from Maui (OGG) to Kona (KOA) on the Big Island — premium cabin booking. Private luxury transfer to your Big Island accommodation near Hawaii Volcanoes National Park or Kohala Coast. Morning coffee tasting at a renowned Kona coffee estate — tour the farm, learn about the harvesting process, and taste award-winning single-origin Kona coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration — Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes. Explore the Kilauea Caldera, walk through lava tube caves (Thurston Lava Tube), drive the Chain of Craters Road, and witness volcanic steam vents. A private park ranger or volcanologist guide enhances the experience with expert commentary.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your Big Island resort for a sunset dinner. If lava flow is active and accessible, arrange a private evening lava viewing tour by boat or helicopter for an unforgettable family experience.

meals.breakfast: Kona coffee estate breakfast — freshly brewed Kona coffee, pastries, tropical fruits, and local honey
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch for the park — premium sandwiches, fresh fruit, energy bars, and hydration packs prepared by the resort
meals.dinner: Canoe Restaurant at Mauna Lani or Brown's Beach House at Fairmont Orchid — recommended: Big Island grass-fed beef, fresh catch of the day, and haupia panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: Check National Park Service website for current volcanic activity and trail closures before visiting. Wear closed-toe shoes and bring a light jacket — temperatures at the caldera can be 10–15°F cooler than the coast. Evening lava boat tours must be booked in advance and are weather/activity dependent.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour of the Big Island — soar over active lava flows, Mauna Kea, Waipio Valley, and the dramatic Kohala coastline. A doors-off helicopter experience provides unobstructed aerial photography opportunities. Approximately 2–3 hours with a narrated flight by an expert pilot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling and manta ray encounter at Keauhou Bay — join a premium guided afternoon snorkel tour to swim alongside the gentle giant manta rays that frequent this bay. Snorkel gear, wetsuits, and professional guides included. Suitable for children aged 8 and above with adult supervision.
day_by_day.evening: Stargazing experience at Mauna Kea Summit (if family has older children) or private resort stargazing session — Hawaii sits in one of the world's premier dark-sky zones. A private astronomer leads the family through constellation identification, telescope viewing of planets and galaxies, and Hawaiian star navigation stories.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — eggs any style, loco moco (Big Island style), fresh papaya, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Post-helicopter beachside lunch — fresh ahi poke bowls, coconut shrimp, and tropical smoothies at a Kona waterfront restaurant
meals.dinner: Private beachfront BBQ dinner arranged by the resort — whole grilled fish, prime wagyu steaks, grilled vegetables, and tropical desserts under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours must be booked well in advance; weight limits apply — inform the operator of all passengers' weights at booking. Mauna Kea summit elevation is 13,796 feet — not recommended for young children or those with respiratory conditions. The resort stargazing alternative is equally magical and family-friendly.

day_by_day.morning: Waipio Valley Adventure — descend into the sacred and lush Waipio Valley by private 4WD tour. Explore black sand beaches, towering waterfalls, and ancient taro fields. Learn about the valley's deep significance in Hawaiian royal history from a knowledgeable local guide. Horseback riding option available for older children.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the Kohala Coast for an afternoon of luxury resort relaxation — enjoy the Big Island resort's pools, waterslides (if family-friendly resort), and beachfront amenities. Optional: private surf or paddleboard lesson for the family on a calm Kohala Coast beach.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Big Island luau experience — attend a premium private or semi-private luau featuring traditional imu ceremony, hula performances, fire knife dancing, and a lavish feast. Book the VIP package for front-row seating and personal server.

meals.breakfast: Early resort breakfast before Waipio departure — hearty eggs, fresh fruit, pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Waimea (Kamuela) farm-to-table restaurant on the return from Waipio Valley — recommended: Merriman's Waimea for iconic Big Island cuisine featuring locally sourced ingredients
meals.dinner: Premium Luau feast — kalua pig, lomi lomi salmon, poi, fresh seafood, haupia, and tropical cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Waipio Valley road descent is extremely steep (25% grade) and requires a 4WD vehicle — private tour operators handle this safely. Book Merriman's Waimea for lunch well in advance as it is very popular. Luau booking should be confirmed at least 1 week ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the Big Island — wake up early for a peaceful sunrise beach walk. Enjoy a leisurely farewell breakfast at the resort. Last-minute luxury souvenir shopping — visit a curated local artisan market or resort boutique for authentic Hawaiian gifts: Kona coffee, macadamia nut products, Niihau shell jewelry, and local artwork.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Kona International Airport (KOA) or inter-island connection as needed. Allow ample time for check-in and security. Enjoy the airport lounge amenities while awaiting departure.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Hawaii with unforgettable memories. If flight schedule allows, enjoy a final farewell dinner at the airport or a nearby restaurant before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the resort — full Hawaiian spread: fresh tropical fruits, macadamia nut waffles, smoked fish platter, eggs Benedict, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or airport lounge — poke bowl, fresh salad, and tropical juice
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or pre-flight restaurant — light and fresh Hawaiian fare for comfortable travel

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer at least 3 hours before departure. Confirm all inter-island and return flight bookings. Pack any liquid food items (Kona coffee, honey, macadamia nuts) in checked luggage per TSA guidelines. Resort concierge can assist with luggage storage if checkout is before the flight. Mahalo for an incredible 10-day Hawaiian adventure!
